items.stem: Why is the potential of the Earth taken as zero?
items.answer: The Earth is a very large conductor; adding or removing charge hardly changes its potential, so it is a convenient reference.

items.stem: Why is charge density larger at the pointed ends of a conductor?
items.answer: σ ∝ 1/R for connected parts; sharp points have small radius of curvature, so σ and the field there are large.
